Hi Ava,

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement and legal reviewed the draft order form and we have a substantive concern around the indemnity language (Section 6): Cedar Health is not comfortable accepting broad third-party IP risk for model output. Specifically: 

- We need clarity on whether Redwood will indemnify for third-party claims alleging infringement by generated output (not just your underlying models).
- If Redwood will defend, we want a liability cap tied to the Order Form value and an exceptions list for open-source components.

I'm attaching our current order form with the redlines (CedarHealth_OrderForm_v3.pdf). Can you confirm Redwood's position and share suggested edits? Procurement would like a short call this week to resolve.

Sam — thanks for the note and for the marked-up form. Appreciate the clarity.

Quick response before legal digs in: Redwood is open to limited indemnity for third-party IP claims tied to model outputs, but we generally:
- Carve out customer-provided data and customer prompts that introduce infringing content;
- Seek a commercially reasonable cap (suggesting 1x ARR or an Order Form value-based cap) rather than unlimited exposure;
- Prefer to control defense for consistency and to preserve settlement flexibility.

I asked Kimberly to provide proposed redlines and an explanation of the tradeoffs — she is copied.

Can we schedule 30 minutes on Tuesday (Mar 15) 10:00–10:30 PT to walk through? I will bring Ben for commercial context.

Subject: RE: Order form redlines + indemnity ask — proposed legal language and rationale

Ava / Ben — see my draft language and commentary below (I pasted the relevant Section 6 edits inline). I kept the changes narrow to preserve operational control while addressing Cedar's concerns.

--- Suggested clause (Order Form playbook style) ---
6. Indemnification and Third-Party Claims
6.1 Redwood will defend and indemnify Customer against any third-party claim alleging that Redwood's models or model-provided software (as delivered by Redwood) infringe a third party's intellectual property, provided that: (a) Customer notifies Redwood promptly of the claim; (b) Customer gives Redwood sole control of the defense and settlement; and (c) the claim does not arise from Customer Content, Customer prompts that incorporate third-party proprietary material, or Customer's use of output in a manner not permitted by the Agreement.
6.2 Notwithstanding the foregoing, Redwood's liability for indemnification under Section 6.1 shall be subject to a cap equal to the total amounts paid by Customer to Redwood under the Order Form in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim ("Indemnity Cap").
6.3 Open source and third-party components that are expressly identified in Attachment A are excluded from Redwood's indemnity obligations.

Commentary (short): the Indemnity Cap ties the exposure to the commercial relationship, which is a common compromise in exchanges like this. We recommend adding a short list of excluded OSS components or a process to identify them during commercial review. Also propose a limited time window for notice (30 days after claim asserted) — we can discuss risk of late notice.

Attachments: redlines_Cedar_3p-claim_track_changes.docx (contains tracked changes and an alternate version with a 2x ARR cap for discussion).

Kimberly / Ava — thanks for the quick turnaround. A couple of counterpoints from Cedar Health's outside counsel: 

1) Defense control: Cedar will accept Redwood leading technical remediation but insists on co-control of litigation decisions involving major settlements or injunctions — client needs approval rights for settlement terms that materially affect patient safety or operations.

2) Cap calibration: a 12-month revenue cap may be lower than Cedar's commercial comfort; they prefer a fixed multiple of annual fees (they suggested 2x annual fees) or a per-claim floor. We'd be open to an insurance-backed approach (Redwood’s E&O policy) as part of the mitigation.

3) OSS carveouts: Cedar proposes a narrower OSS carveout (only components listed in an agreed appendix) rather than a broad ‘identified in Attachment A’ approach. They want an onboarding checklist to confirm which components are in scope.

I'll attach our redlines. Let's keep the call (Ava proposed Mar 15) and use it to resolve defense-control mechanics and cap numbers.

Regards,
Eve Dunlop
